title: Copilot Studio: Azure SQL tables and views as an agent knowledge source
summary: Hold: the credit-control navigation omits the Products group and the actual tenant-capacity checkbox. The briefing also treats data-policy applicability as unconfirmed even though Microsoft's platform documentation covers the Power Platform SQL connection this source uses.

claims.where: What's changing: roadmap description and title
claims.claim: The roadmap title describes SQL server support, while its description plans Azure SQL knowledge for Copilot Studio agents.
claims.quote: The Azure SQL Knowledge Source capability extends the range of enterprise data sources that makers can leverage when building agents in Copilot Studio.

claims.where: front matter: status; What's changing; Open questions
claims.claim: The roadmap status remains In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development", "statusKey": "in-development"

claims.where: front matter: targetDate; What's changing; Open questions
claims.claim: The general availability target is September CY2026, already past on the run date.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "September CY2026"

claims.where: front matter: previewDate; What's changing; Open questions
claims.claim: The preview target is August CY2026, already past on the run date.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "August CY2026"

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant) is the only cloud listed in the record.
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.where: front matter: platforms; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The record lists the Web platform.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Web"]

claims.where: front matter: releasePhase; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The release phases are Current Channel, General Availability and Preview.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["Current Channel", "General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.where: front matter: products
claims.claim: The roadmap product is Microsoft Copilot Studio.
claims.quote: "products": ["Microsoft Copilot Studio"]

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents adding Azure SQL tables and views as agent knowledge in the Microsoft Copilot experience.
claims.quote:
Add Azure SQL tables and views as a knowledge source (Microsoft Copilot)
You can add Azure SQL tables and views as a knowledge source in Copilot Studio.

claims.where: What's changing: maker setup
claims.claim: A maker uses Build > Knowledge, selects Azure SQL or SQL Server in Add knowledge, selects a connection and objects, and selects Add to agent.
claims.quote:
Select the Build tab.
In the components panel, select Knowledge.
In the Add knowledge dialog, select Azure SQL (or SQL Server, depending on the label shown in your environment).

claims.where: What's changing: publication
claims.claim: The agent must be published for the knowledge source to be available in the published experience.
claims.quote: Publish the agent so the knowledge source is available in the published experience.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The agent answers questions by reading structured database data through the configured connection and database permissions.
claims.quote: Your agent can answer questions by reading structured data from your Azure SQL database, using the configured connection and database permissions.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure, views
claims.claim: Views appear in the same selection list as tables.
claims.quote: Views appear in the same selection list as tables. You don't need a separate knowledge source type to add a view.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope
claims.claim: The SQL connection identity needs database access and permission to list and read the selected tables and views.
claims.quote: The identity you use to authenticate the SQL connection must have permission to access the database and list and read the selected tables and views.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Power Platform must be able to reach Azure SQL through configured networking, such as firewall rules allowing Azure services or private connectivity.
claims.quote: Network access configured so Power Platform can reach your Azure SQL server. For example, use firewall rules that allow Azure services, or private connectivity as required by your organization.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Licence; Scope
claims.claim: The source's prerequisites name an Azure SQL Database or Azure SQL Managed Instance reachable from Power Platform.
claims.quote: An Azure SQL Database or Azure SQL Managed Instance that your organization can reach from Power Platform.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing: Licence; Scope
claims.claim: Setup requires access to Copilot Studio and permission to edit the agent.
claims.quote: Access to Copilot Studio and permission to edit the agent.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Licence
claims.claim: The Azure SQL feature page's prerequisites name no licence.
claims.quote: Prerequisites: An Azure SQL Database or Azure SQL Managed Instance; Credentials that can connect to the database and list and read the tables and views; Access to Copilot Studio and permission to edit the agent; Network access configured so Power Platform can reach your Azure SQL server.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Azure SQL knowledge uses a Power Platform SQL connection and at runtime relies on the agent user's Microsoft authentication and access through that connection path.
claims.quote: Azure SQL knowledge uses the Power Platform SQL connection you create or select during setup. At runtime, the agent relies on the agent user's Microsoft authentication and the access granted through that connection path.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk and impact
claims.claim: Users' answers are grounded in data accessible through the maker's configured connection and database permissions.
claims.quote: Users only receive answers based on data the maker can access through the maker's configured connection and database permissions.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity, SQL authentication
claims.claim: SQL Server authentication is an option, with permissions applying to the SQL user specified when creating the connection.
claims.quote: For SQL Server authentication, permissions apply to the SQL user you specify when you create the connection.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft does not fully spell out which identity reaches the database for each runtime question.
claims.quote: Searched: Azure SQL knowledge runtime identity write actions standard harness SQL Server support; "Azure SQL" "knowledge" "identity" "runtime". Read knowledge-add-azure-sql-tables and knowledge-graph-vs-power-platform-connectors; neither resolves the feature page's dual identity wording.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The Azure SQL knowledge feature page documents reading structured data, but no write action.
claims.quote: Searched: Azure SQL knowledge runtime identity write actions standard harness SQL Server support. Read the complete knowledge-add-azure-sql-tables page; its operations add, select and read knowledge, with no database write action documented for this source.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The knowledge source's name and description help the agent determine when to use it.
claims.quote: Clear names and descriptions help the agent determine when and how to use your Azure SQL data.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support, first sentence
claims.claim: Setup fails quietly when permissions or networking are wrong.
claims.quote: Searched: Azure SQL knowledge runtime identity write actions standard harness SQL Server support. Read knowledge-add-azure-sql-tables: insufficient permissions can hide objects, and network access is required, but silent failure for permissions or networking is not stated.
claims.fix: Replace 'Setup fails quietly when permissions or networking are wrong:' with 'Missing or insufficient permissions can hide database objects during setup:'. Keep the existing, separately supported network prerequisite.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support, missing objects
claims.claim: Insufficient connection permissions can prevent database objects from appearing during setup.
claims.quote: Missing or insufficient permissions can prevent servers, databases, tables, or views from appearing during setup.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support, primary key
claims.claim: Microsoft requires a primary key for each table.
claims.quote: Define a primary key for each table. The agent uses primary keys to identify rows and return results.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support, column names
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends clear, descriptive column names.
claims.quote: Use clear, descriptive column names in tables and views to help the agent understand the data. Avoid cryptic abbreviations.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing: Meter
claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot harness agents use consumption-based billing measured in Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Usage is billed based on consumption and measured in Copilot Credits. Creating and using agents, workflows, and apps consumes credits based on usage and rate of consumption.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Cost and licensing: Meter
claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot harness billing starts during building, and building and testing can consume credits.
claims.quote: The Microsoft Copilot harness charges credits from the moment you start building. Experiences such as creating an automated solution with natural language, previewing and testing an agent, and generating and creating agent evaluations all consume credits.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Meter; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Credits cover LLM tokens, tools including knowledge and MCPs, and the Microsoft Copilot harness itself.
claims.quote: For experiences powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness, Copilot Credits are charged for large language model (LLM) tokens, tools (including knowledge and MCPs), and the harness itself.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Meter
claims.claim: This Microsoft Copilot harness usage is not included with a user's Microsoft 365 Copilot licence.
claims.quote: Agents powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness use consumption-based billing. Building, testing, evaluating, and running these agents can consume Copilot Credits. This usage isn't included with a user's Microsoft 365 Copilot license.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Meter
claims.claim: Credits are charged to the runtime environment from prepaid capacity or its linked pay-as-you-go plan.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits are charged to the environment where the agent runs, from prepaid capacity or through the environment's pay-as-you-go billing plan, and not to the individual makers or users who run agents.

claims.where: front matter: cost; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The variable cost rating corresponds to the documented Copilot Credits meter.
claims.quote: Usage is billed based on consumption and measured in Copilot Credits.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: An Azure SQL knowledge-specific Copilot Credit rate is not published.
claims.quote: Searched: Azure SQL knowledge Copilot Credits rate pricing Microsoft Copilot harness; "Azure SQL" "knowledge" "rate" "Credits". Read billing-credit-overview, manage-usage-github-copilot-harness and the Azure SQL feature page; no source-specific rate found.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Controls and gaps
claims.claim: The standard-harness connector comparison says availability might depend on standard versus premium connectors and the Copilot Studio plan.
claims.quote:
This article describes features used in agents or agent flows powered by the standard harness.
Power Platform connectors: Availability might depend on standard vs. premium connectors and Copilot Studio plan; governed via Power Platform DLP.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Controls and gaps, plan qualification
claims.claim: The reviewed documentation does not establish that the standard-harness connector plan qualification applies to this Microsoft Copilot harness source.
claims.quote: Searched: Azure SQL knowledge Copilot Credits rate pricing Microsoft Copilot harness. Read knowledge-graph-vs-power-platform-connectors, knowledge-add-azure-sql-tables, billing-credit-overview and manage-usage-github-copilot-harness; no such feature-specific plan qualification found.

claims.where: What's changing: Learn status
claims.claim: The Azure SQL feature page supplies no release date or rollout status.
claims.quote: Searched: Azure SQL knowledge Microsoft Copilot admin enable disable default data policy SQL connector. Read the complete knowledge-add-azure-sql-tables page; it documents setup and permissions but contains no release date or rollout status.

claims.where: Scope: other harnesses
claims.claim: The cited Azure SQL feature page does not specify whether this source also appears on other harnesses.
claims.quote: Searched: Azure SQL knowledge runtime identity write actions standard harness SQL Server support. Read knowledge-add-azure-sql-tables and knowledge-graph-vs-power-platform-connectors; the feature page itself does not give a cross-harness availability statement.

claims.where: Scope: SQL Server qualification; Open questions
claims.claim: The feature page's preparation section names Azure SQL databases or SQL Server, while its prerequisites name Azure SQL Database or Azure SQL Managed Instance.
claims.quote:
An Azure SQL Database or Azure SQL Managed Instance that your organization can reach from Power Platform.
Copilot Studio agents support Azure SQL databases or SQL Server.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, maker access
claims.claim: The Microsoft Copilot harness has no separate maker-access setting and uses existing Copilot Studio and environment permissions.
claims.quote: The Microsoft Copilot harness doesn't have its own maker-access setting. To control who can create agents, use your existing Copilot Studio and environment permissions.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout, diagnostic view
claims.claim: Microsoft suggests testing with a diagnostic view containing a small known dataset before production data.
claims.quote: Create a diagnostic view in Azure SQL that returns a small, known dataset. Confirm that the connection identity can list and read the view, then select it as a knowledge source. Test questions about that dataset before using production data.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout, consumption monitoring
claims.claim: Administrators can monitor Copilot Credit consumption in the Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote: Use the Copilot Studio licensing pages in the Power Platform admin center to review consumption at multiple levels:

claims.where: controls[0].ui
claims.claim: The general connector-blocking UI is Security > Data and privacy > Data policy > New Policy > Next > Next > connector menu > Block.
claims.quote:
Select Next. The Add an environment page appears.
To add an environment to your data policy, select the environment in the Available tab, and then select Add to policy.
Select Next. The Assign connectors page appears.
claims.fix: Include the omitted scope selections in both copies of this path: 'Security > Data and privacy > Data policy > New Policy > Next > Available > environment > Add to policy > Next > connector > three-dot menu > Block'. The cited page also requires finishing the wizard with Create policy or Update policy.

claims.where: controls[0].api
claims.claim: Microsoft.PowerApps.Administration.PowerShell provides Add-ConnectorsToPolicy with PolicyName, Connectors and Classification to classify connectors in a DLP policy.
claims.quote:
Add-ConnectorsToPolicy
    [-PolicyName] <String>
    [-Classification] <String>
    [-Connectors] <Object[]>
    [[-ApiVersion] <String>]
    [<CommonParameters>]

claims.where: controls[1].ui
claims.claim: The credit-control path goes directly from Licensing to Copilot Studio and from Capacity overages to Save.
claims.quote:
Under Products, select Copilot Studio, and then select Manage Copilot Credits.
Under Capacity overages, select or clear Draw from the available capacity in my tenant to control what happens when the environment exhausts its allocation:
claims.fix: Replace both copies of controls[1].ui.path with 'Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Manage Copilot Credits > environment > Allocate capacity > Capacity overages > Draw from the available capacity in my tenant > Save'.

claims.where: controls[1].api
claims.claim: PUT https://api.powerplatform.com/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=2024-10-01 accepts scope.environmentId and allocatedEntitlements containing MCSMessages, allocation.quantity and a TenantPool enforcement rule.
claims.quote:
Invoke-RestMethod -Method Put `
    -Uri "$apiBaseUrl/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=$apiVersion" `
    -Headers $headers -ContentType "application/json" -Body $allocationBody

claims.where: Governance controls: data-policy roles
claims.claim: The cited data-policy instructions require a tenant admin or Environment Admin.
claims.quote: Be a tenant admin or have the Environment Admin role.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls: capacity roles
claims.claim: Managing capacity requires Power Platform Administrator, Global Administrator or an equivalent role that can manage licensing and capacity.
claims.quote: Permission to manage licensing and capacity. Sign in as a user with the Power Platform Administrator or Global Administrator role, or an equivalent role that can manage licensing and capacity.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Cost and licensing: Controls and gaps
claims.claim: The environment capacity controls apply across Copilot Studio workloads, not just Azure SQL knowledge.
claims.quote: The capacity and consumption controls in the Power Platform admin center apply across Copilot Studio. They aren't exclusive to the Microsoft Copilot harness. Configure controls with the other Copilot Studio agents, workflows, and features in mind for each environment.

claims.where: Governance controls: spend versus access
claims.claim: Credit controls govern consumption, not authoring access.
claims.quote: Credit allocations and agent limits control consumption. They don't control who is an approved author or who can open the Copilot Studio portal.

claims.where: Governance controls: allocation boundary
claims.claim: An environment allocation is not a spending boundary if tenant capacity or linked pay-as-you-go remains available.
claims.quote: An allocation isn't a boundary if the environment can continue drawing from tenant capacity or pay-as-you-go billing.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Controls and gaps, per-agent limit
claims.claim: A per-agent monthly Copilot Credit limit is documented in the Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote:
Select Manage Agents.
Select the agent, and then select Set limit.
Enter the monthly Copilot Credit limit.
Configure the notification threshold.
Turn on Stop usage if the agent should be turned off when it reaches the limit.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Controls and gaps, Azure alerts
claims.claim: Azure budgets and alerts notify but do not stop Copilot Studio consumption.
claims.quote: Azure budgets and alerts send notifications but don't stop Copilot Studio consumption.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls; Open questions: data-policy applicability
claims.claim: Microsoft has not confirmed that Power Platform data policies apply to this Azure SQL knowledge source.
claims.quote: A core component of Power Apps, Power Automate, and Microsoft Copilot Studio is the use of connectors to enumerate, populate, push, and pull data. Power Platform admin center data policies allow administrators to control access to these connectors
claims.fix: Replace 'Treat the data policy row as a general control until Microsoft confirms it applies to this source' with 'Power Platform data policies govern connector access; this source uses a Power Platform SQL connection.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/wp-data-loss-prevention alongside the existing Azure SQL feature source. In Open questions, remove 'Does a Power Platform data policy block this knowledge source, and' and retain the narrower question about which connector entry to classify.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls: exact connector classification
claims.claim: The feature-specific documentation does not identify the exact connector entry to classify for Azure SQL knowledge in the Microsoft Copilot experience.
claims.quote: Searched: "Azure SQL" "knowledge" "data policies" "Microsoft Copilot"; Power Platform data policies SQL connection knowledge Microsoft Copilot harness connectors enforcement. Read knowledge-add-azure-sql-tables, admin-data-loss-prevention and wp-data-loss-prevention; no feature-specific entry found.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The source is maker opt-in: the maker chooses and adds it to an agent.
claims.quote:
Locate one or more tables or views to add. Tables and views appear in the same selection list.
Select Add to agent to finish adding the knowledge source.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters: arrival and default
claims.claim: Microsoft does not state that this source is automatically added or changes existing agents by default.
claims.quote: Searched: Azure SQL knowledge Microsoft Copilot admin enable disable default data policy SQL connector. Read the roadmap record, knowledge-add-azure-sql-tables and knowledge-sources-overview; no automatic addition or change to existing agents stated.

claims.where: Why it matters: dedicated admin switch
claims.claim: No dedicated Azure SQL knowledge enablement switch is documented separately from general governance controls.
claims.quote: Searched: Azure SQL knowledge Microsoft Copilot admin enable disable default data policy SQL connector; "Knowledge sources for agents" "Azure SQL". Read feature and knowledge-add-existing-copilot pages; knowledge-sources-for-agents-rule search lists SharePoint, websites and documents, not SQL.

claims.where: Governance guidance: maker permissions, database controls and consumption monitoring
claims.claim: The governance checklist names controls that are not represented in the controls table.
claims.quote: Identify ... which makers can edit agents there; Ask database owners to create a dedicated identity and views ... confirm the firewall or private connectivity route; Watch credit consumption ... The table contains only data-policy classification and environment credit allocation.
claims.fix: The checklist's authoring-permission review, database permission/view/network review and consumption-monitoring steps have no corresponding controls-table rows. Do not add rows as part of this correction.
